legend: Little Paul wants to learn how to play piano. He already has a melody he wants to start with. For simplicity he represented this melody as a sequence a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ of key numbers: the more a number is, the closer it is to the right end of the piano keyboard.

Paul is very clever and knows that the essential thing is to properly assign fingers to notes he's going to play. If he chooses an inconvenient fingering, he will then waste a lot of time trying to learn how to play the melody by these fingers and he will probably not succeed.

Let's denote the fingers of hand by numbers from 1$$$1$$$ to 5$$$5$$$. We call a fingering any sequence b1,…,bn$$$b_1, \ldots, b_n$$$ of fingers numbers. A fingering is convenient if for all 1≤i≤n−1$$$1\leq i \leq n - 1$$$ the following holds:
if ai<ai+1$$$a_i  \lt  a_{i+1}$$$ then bi<bi+1$$$b_i  \lt  b_{i+1}$$$, because otherwise Paul needs to take his hand off the keyboard to play the (i+1)$$$(i+1)$$$-st note;
if ai>ai+1$$$a_i  \gt  a_{i+1}$$$ then bi>bi+1$$$b_i  \gt  b_{i+1}$$$, because of the same;

if ai=ai+1$$$a_i = a_{i+1}$$$ then bi≠bi+1$$$b_i\neq b_{i+1}$$$, because using the same finger twice in a row is dumb. Please note that there is ≠$$$\neq$$$, not =$$$=$$$ between bi$$$b_i$$$ and bi+1$$$b_{i+1}$$$.
Please provide any convenient fingering or find out that there is none.
input: The first line contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤105$$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$) denoting the number of notes.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤2⋅105$$$1 \le a_i \le 2\cdot10^5$$$) denoting the positions of notes on the keyboard.
output: If there is no convenient fingering, print −1$$$-1$$$. Otherwise, print n$$$n$$$ numbers b1,b2,…,bn$$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$$$, each from 1$$$1$$$ to 5$$$5$$$, denoting a convenient fingering, separated by spaces.
note: The third sample test is kinda "Non stop" song by Reflex.

legend.ai: 小保罗想学习如何弹钢琴。他已经有一段想从中开始练习的旋律。为简单起见，他将这段旋律表示为一个由琴键编号组成的序列 a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$：编号越大，就越靠近钢琴键盘的右端。
保罗非常聪明，知道关键在于为将要弹奏的音符正确分配手指。如果他选择了不合适的指法，那么他会浪费大量时间尝试用这些手指学会弹奏这段旋律，而且很可能无法成功。
我们用从 1$$$1$$$ 到 5$$$5$$$ 的数字表示手指。我们称任意一个由手指编号组成的序列 b1,…,bn$$$b_1, \ldots, b_n$$$ 为一种指法。当对于所有 1≤i≤n−1$$$1\leq i \leq n - 1$$$ 都满足以下条件时，这种指法是合适的：
如果 ai<ai+1$$$a_i  \lt  a_{i+1}$$$，那么 bi<bi+1$$$b_i  \lt  b_{i+1}$$$，否则保罗就需要将手从键盘上移开才能弹奏第 (i+1)$$$(i+1)$$$ 个音符；
如果 ai>ai+1$$$a_i  \gt  a_{i+1}$$$，那么 bi>bi+1$$$b_i  \gt  b_{i+1}$$$，原因相同；
如果 ai=ai+1$$$a_i = a_{i+1}$$$，那么 bi≠bi+1$$$b_i\neq b_{i+1}$$$，因为连续两次使用同一根手指是不明智的。请注意，bi$$$b_i$$$ 与 bi+1$$$b_{i+1}$$$ 之间是 ≠$$$\neq$$$，而不是 =$$$=$$$。
请给出任意一种方便的指法，或者确定不存在这样的指法。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤105$$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$)，表示音符的数量。
第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数 a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$(1≤ai≤2⋅105$$$1 \le a_i \le 2\cdot10^5$$$)，表示音符在键盘上的位置。

output.ai: 如果不存在方便的指法，则输出 −1$$$-1$$$。否则，输出 n$$$n$$$ 个数 b1,b2,…,bn$$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$$$，每个数在 1$$$1$$$ 到 5$$$5$$$ 之间，表示一种方便的指法，用空格分隔。

note.ai: 第三个样例测试有点像 Reflex 的歌曲 "Non stop"。
